_what: fusion's per-project configuration for THIS project. fusion reads it from the project root and merges it over fusion's own built-in defaults. Today it configures ONE thing, the non-Markdown paths your project declares as citation-bearing — see _citations. Keys the parser does not recognise are carried through untouched and never reported, which is why these underscore-prefixed notes can live in the file itself. The one exception is something fusion has RETIRED — a file or a key that used to configure something and no longer does. A retired file or key is reported on every guarded tool call until you delete it, because something that is inert AND silent would leave you believing a setting is in force when the mechanism behind it is gone. See _retired for the ones that exist today.
_override: To change something, add the key you want to change, in the shape fusion documents for it. The merge is per LEAF, not per object: a key you declare is taken exactly as you wrote it, and a key you leave out — even inside an object you did declare — falls straight through to fusion's built-in default. There are TWO layers, this file and those defaults. The plugin-level layer that used to sit between them, the plugin's own hooks/config.json, is gone with the guard settings it carried, so nothing stands between what you write here and what fusion ships. So {"citations": {"extraPaths": ["internal/*.go"]}} sets the citation paths and touches nothing else, and a leaf you omit is fusion's own value rather than something inherited from an install. A value with the wrong type is dropped and named in an advisory, then inherits as if you had omitted it; a file that is not valid JSON is dropped and reported the same way, never ignored in silence.
_citations: Which of your NON-MARKDOWN files carry record citations is something only your project knows, so your project declares it here and fusion detects nothing. "citations": {"extraPaths": ["src/**/*.go", "internal/*.py"]} names the files that bin/fusion-citation-check and bin/fusion-citation-sweep read IN ADDITION to the Markdown they already read. Each entry is a git pathspec evaluated under :(glob), so * does not cross a / and ** does, and it is resolved against the files git tracks — an untracked or an ignored file is never named by one. Declaring a file is a judgement you make and not one fusion can make for you: outside Markdown there is no code fence and no block quote, so fusion cannot tell a token that POINTS at a record from one that merely shows what a record name looks like, and inside a file you declare it reads every such token as a pointer. Declare the files that cite records, and leave out the ones that exhibit them. DECLARE NOTHING AND YOU GET [], which is exactly today's behaviour: the Markdown corpus alone, no extra files, no advisory. The value must be an array of strings with none of them empty; anything else is dropped WHOLE and named in an advisory, then inherits as if you had omitted it, so one bad entry never leaves half a declaration in force.
_retired: Two kinds of thing are retired, and each is reported on every guarded tool call until you delete it. A FILE: if your project root still carries a fusion-guard.json, this file replaced it and fusion no longer reads a byte of it — copy nothing across, since everything that file could set is now retired too, then delete it and the advisory naming it stops. KEYS inside this file: the four top-level keys that held the guard — guard, decisions, escalation and, since 260824, churn — and the two leaves of the orchestrator container, orchestrator.maxTurns, which went with the Phase-2 Turn loop on 260910, and orchestrator.dispatchMinutes, which went with the dispatch bound the same day. A retired leaf is named on its own so that a Turn budget and a stopping time are each answered as the separate intention somebody wrote down; neither has a replacement to move to, and the orchestrator container now holds nothing but these two retirements.
_gitTracked: This file belongs in version control, and that is the point of it living at the project root. It decides which of your files fusion's citation helpers read — so every change to it has to appear in a diff and pass through the same review as the rest of the project. The diff is now the ONLY thing that bounds it. fusion used to defend this file against its own agents: the guard added it to the protected list as soon as it existed and wrote back any change an agent made to it. That defence went with the protected-path mechanism, so an agent can edit this file like any other, and the git history is where you see that one did.
